items.title: v2.1.162
items.bullet_md: - 🛠 **[v2.1.162](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/releases/tag/v2.1.162)** — _Claude Code releases_. — Claude Code 2.1.162 adds waitingFor to agent --json output for viewing blocked sessions and restores Grep/Glob as explicit --allowedTools options on native builds — though the opt-in only works from CLI args, not from settings.json permission rules, so teams cannot persist the preference across projects without shell wrappers.

score_components.taste_reason: Actionable Claude Code release (v2.1.162) extending state-of-ai's Claude Code row — `waitingFor` for agent blocking and explicit Grep/Glob tools are real workflow improvements for daily users.

items.title: JetBrains releases Mellum2, a 12B open-source coding model that runs like a 2.5B
items.bullet_md: - 📧 **[JetBrains releases Mellum2, a 12B open-source coding model that runs like a 2.5B](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.31268)** — _AlphaSignal_. — Mellum2's MoE uses 64 experts with 8 active per token and a 131K context window, shipping six Apache 2.0 variants including a Thinking model scoring 69.9% on LiveCodeBench v6 — JetBrains trained from scratch on 10.6 trillion tokens with speculative decoding via a multi-token prediction head for IDE-speed inference.

score_components.taste_reason: Mellum2: 12B coding model at 2.5B inference speed from JetBrains — concrete specs and credible vendor, directly relevant to IDE coding workflows.

items.title: Direct Preference Optimization Beyond Chatbots
items.bullet_md: - 🟡 **[Direct Preference Optimization Beyond Chatbots](https://huggingface.co/blog/Dharma-AI/direct-preference-optimization-beyond-chatbots)** — _Hugging Face blog_. — Dharma-AI used DPO to cut OCR text degeneration by 59.4% on average across five vision-language model families by training on the model's own degenerate outputs as rejection pairs — SFT alone had a structural ceiling on the failure mode that DPO's completion-level loss bypasses.

score_components.taste_reason: Technical ML content (DPO beyond chatbots) from Hugging Face blog is on-topic but the title is vague on specifics — no concrete results or benchmarks cited.

items.title: New paper explains why bigger models learn rare tasks that smaller ones never can
items.bullet_md: - 📧 **[New paper explains why bigger models learn rare tasks that smaller ones never can](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.29548)** — _AlphaSignal_. — ArXiv:2605.29548 shows larger models retain rare tasks via reduced gradient interference — OLMo experiments from 4M to 4B params confirmed that smaller models' neurons get consumed by high-frequency patterns, while wider models let rare-task gradients accumulate without being overwritten by common-task updates.

score_components.taste_reason: Theoretical analysis of scaling and emergent capabilities — interesting framing but no specific results or actionable takeaways.

items.title: Off-Distribution Voices: Fanfiction Subgenres as Universal Vernacular Jailbreaks for Aligned LLMs
items.bullet_md: - 🧪 **[Off-Distribution Voices: Fanfiction Subgenres as Universal Vernacular Jailbreaks for Aligned LLMs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.04483)** — _arXiv cs.CL_. — The paper reports mean ASR of 0.731 across eight models using twelve AO3 subgenres as carriers — tripling existing baselines — with the four-turn Saga-A4 pipeline reaching 0.924, and finds that two active defenses widen the vulnerability gap rather than close it.

score_components.taste_reason: Novel finding: real fanfiction subgenres serve as universal jailbreak carriers by exploiting a creative-writing register safety training misses. Concrete security implication with a novel attack vector.

items.title: AI Isn't What's Driving Your Defect Rate
